q_44958.question_text: What will the first reported earnings per share after June 2026 be for the following companies? (SpaceX)
q_44958.reasoning:
# Analysis of SpaceX Q2 2026 Earnings Per Share

## (a) Time left until resolution
**10 days.** The earnings report is scheduled for August 4, 2026, and today is July 25, 2026. This is an extremely short timeline with high certainty about the timing.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides a clear analyst estimate: **Benzinga Pro estimates SpaceX will report a loss of 25 cents per share (-$0.25)** for Q2 2026.

Given that:
- This is the company's first public earnings report (IPO was June 12, 2026)
- The date and estimate come from professional research platforms (Benzinga Pro)
- There are only 10 days until the actual report
- The estimate is specific and based on structured analyst consensus

The most likely outcome is that the actual EPS will be very close to this consensus estimate, with some deviation possible but limited.

## (c) What would push the value lower (more negative/larger loss)?

- **Unexpected operational challenges** discovered during the reporting period
- **Revenue shortfall** relative to the $6.98B estimate
- **One-time charges** or write-downs related to the IPO or early operational phases
- **Higher-than-expected operating expenses** during the quarter
- **Conservative accounting** choices in the first public report
- Broader aerospace/space industry headwinds not yet reflected in estimates

## (d) What would push the value higher (less negative/smaller loss or profit)?

- **Better-than-expected launch cadence** or commercial revenue performance
- **Cost controls** exceeding initial projections
- **Government contracts** coming through ahead of schedule
- **Satellite deployment revenue** accelerating faster than modeled
- **Benefit from scale** in manufacturing or operations
- Analysts' estimate being somewhat pessimistic on a newly-public company

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**Specific cited source:** Benzinga Pro estimates: **-$0.25 per share** on revenue of $6.98 billion.

This is the only quantified analyst estimate provided in the research. For a newly public company with only 10 days until earnings, this consensus estimate is the strongest available reference point. 

Historical context: Early earnings of newly-IPO'd companies often show losses or thin margins during scaling phases, which is consistent with the negative EPS estimate here. SpaceX's business model (capital-intensive, long development cycles) would support losses in early public reporting.

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

Given:
- The analyst consensus of -$0.25 is based on current available information
- Time to resolution is only 10 days (minimal time for surprises)
- This is a measured financial metric with defined reporting standards
- Standard earnings report variance is typically within 10-15% of estimates for large companies

I will construct a distribution centered on the -$0.25 estimate with modest dispersion:

- **Median (50th percentile):** -$0.25 (the consensus estimate)
- **Distribution shape:** Slightly wider than a normal distribution to account for potential operational surprises in a newly-public company, but not extremely wide given the short timeframe
- **10th percentile (lower tail):** Around -$0.40 to -$0.45 (significant operational challenges)
- **90th percentile (upper tail):** Around -$0.10 to -$0.05 (better performance than expected)

The range provided (-1.005 to 0.505) is quite wide, allowing for various scenarios. My distribution will be concentrated near the consensus estimate but allow for meaningful deviations.

---

Low (10th percentile): -0.42
Median (50th percentile): -0.25
High (90th percentile): -0.08
q_44958.research_text:
SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) is scheduled to report its first public earnings for the second quarter of 2026 after market close on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. The company will host a live audio-only webcast at 4:30 p.m. ET to discuss the results [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/07/60612760/quick-spark-spacex-to-report-first-public-earnings-on-august-4-details-and-estimates-inside), [teslaoracle.com](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/07/21/spacex-spcx-announces-the-date-for-its-first-ever-earnings-call-and-financial-results-q2-2026/).

Benzinga Pro estimates SpaceX will report a loss of 25 cents per share on quarterly revenue of $6.98 billion [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/07/60612760/quick-spark-spacex-to-report-first-public-earnings-on-august-4-details-and-estimates-inside). This earnings report is particularly significant as it triggers the first wave of early-release-eligible shares to become tradable on August 6, 2026 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/22/spacex-earnings-are-coming-aug-4/), with approximately 911.5 million shares becoming eligible for sale [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/spacex-sets-august-4-for-first-ever-earnings-report-triggering-116-billion-lock-up-expiration/). SpaceX went public on June 12, 2026, at $135 per share [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/22/spacex-earnings-are-coming-aug-4/). The stock has experienced post-IPO volatility, trading at $123.54 on July 22, down 45% from its June 16 peak of $225.64 [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/spacex-sets-august-4-for-first-ever-earnings-report-triggering-116-billion-lock-up-expiration/).
